statement: For strictly positive probability distributions, the intersection rule of conditional independence holds: if $X \perp\!\!\!\perp Y \mid Z,W$ and $X \perp\!\!\!\perp W \mid Z,Y$, then $X \perp\!\!\!\perp W,Y \mid Z$.

symbols.meaning: Conditional probability of A given B

steps.text: Express the given conditional independence assumptions $X \perp\!\!\!\perp Y \mid Z,W$ and $X \perp\!\!\!\perp W \mid Z,Y$ as equalities of conditional probabilities: $P(X \mid Z,W,Y) = P(X \mid Z,W)$ and $P(X \mid Z,W,Y) = P(X \mid Z,Y)$, which implies $P(X \mid Z,Y) = P(X \mid Z,W)$.
Apply the Law of total probability to $P(X \mid Z)$ by summing over the partition of $W$: $P(X \mid Z) = \sum_{w \in W} P(X \mid Z, W=w) P(W=w \mid Z)$.
Substitute the equality $P(X \mid Z,W) = P(X \mid Y,Z)$ derived in Step 1 into the summation: $P(X \mid Z) = \sum_{w \in W} P(X \mid Y,Z) P(W=w \mid Z)$.
Factor the term $P(X \mid Z,Y)$ out of the summation over $w$: $P(X \mid Z) = P(X \mid Z,Y) \sum_{w \in W} P(W=w \mid Z)$.
Simplify the sum $\sum_{w \in W} P(W=w \mid Z)$ to 1, yielding: $P(X \mid Z) = P(X \mid Z,Y)$.
Combine $P(X \mid Z,W,Y) = P(X \mid Z,Y)$ and $P(X \mid Z,Y) = P(X \mid Z)$ to conclude $P(X \mid Z,W,Y) = P(X \mid Z)$, which is equivalent to the statement $X \perp\!\!\!\perp Y,W \mid Z$.

assumptions.assumption: The joint probability distribution is strictly positive.
assumptions.breaks_when: If any probability of events in the conditioning set is zero, the conditional probabilities are undefined or not uniquely determined.
